# io_uring Basics without the Ceremony

## Thesis

**`io_uring`** is Linux's submission/completion ring for async I/O: you push SQEs (submission queue entries), the kernel does work, and you reap CQEs (completion queue entries) — amortising syscall overhead for chatty I/O. You do not need a framework to understand the shape.

## Mental model

```text
  mmap two rings shared with the kernel
  ┌──────── SQ ────────┐     ┌──────── CQ ────────┐
  │ SQE: op, fd, buf…  │ --> │ CQE: res, user_data│
  └────────────────────┘     └────────────────────┘
  io_uring_enter() wakes / waits when needed
```

Common ops (from `linux/io_uring.h`): `IORING_OP_READV`, `WRITEV`, `FSYNC`, `ACCEPT`, `CONNECT`, …

## Worked example

This box has kernel UAPI headers but **no liburing** and we will not install packages. Header presence:

```text
* If the ring is initialized with IORING_SETUP_SQE128, then
#define IORING_SETUP_IOPOLL	(1U << 0)	/* io_context is polled */
#define IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL	(1U << 1)	/* SQ poll thread */
#define IORING_SETUP_SQ_AFF	(1U << 2)	/* sq_thread_cpu is valid */
#define IORING_SETUP_CQSIZE	(1U << 3)	/* app defines CQ size */
#define IORING_SETUP_CLAMP	(1U << 4)	/* clamp SQ/CQ ring sizes */
#define IORING_SETUP_ATTACH_WQ	(1U << 5)	/* attach to existing wq */
#define IORING_SETUP_R_DISABLED	(1U << 6)	/* start with ring disabled */
#define IORING_SETUP_SUBMIT_ALL	(1U << 7)	/* continue submit on error */
#define IORING_SETUP_COOP_TASKRUN	(1U << 8)
#define IORING_SETUP_TASKRUN_FLAG	(1U << 9)
#define IORING_SETUP_SQE128		(1U << 10) /* SQEs are 128 byte */
#define IORING_SETUP_CQE32		(1U << 11) /* CQEs are 32 byte */
#define IORING_SETUP_SINGLE_ISSUER	(1U << 12)
#define IORING_SETUP_DEFER_TASKRUN	(1U << 13)
```

Minimal conceptual flow with liburing (run on a host that has it):

```c
/* sketch — requires liburing */
#include <liburing.h>
/* io_uring_queue_init(entries, &ring, 0);
   sqe = io_uring_get_sqe(&ring);
   io_uring_prep_read(sqe, fd, buf, len, offset);
   io_uring_submit(&ring);
   io_uring_wait_cqe(&ring, &cqe);
   // cqe->res is bytes or -errno
   io_uring_cqe_seen(&ring, cqe); */
```

Without liburing, the same steps are `io_uring_setup`, mmap of SQ/CQ, fill SQEs, `io_uring_enter`, reap CQEs — see the kernel documentation.

For sequential bulk writes (imagers, installers), io_uring shines when you keep multiple SQEs in flight instead of write-syscall-per-block.

## Trap

**Ignoring `cqe->res < 0`.** Completions report errors as negative errno. Also: mixing registered buffers / fixed files incorrectly; start with plain fds and anonymous buffers.

## Boring rule

Learn the SQE→CQE loop with one `READV`/`WRITEV` before registering buffers or using `IORING_SETUP_SQPOLL`. Prefer a maintained helper (liburing) over hand-rolled mmap unless you are writing a runtime.

## Try this

1. On a lab host: `sudo apt install liburing-dev` (there — not on this bot box) and run the liburing examples.
2. Compare `dd` of a large file with and without an io_uring-based copy tool.
3. Read `IORING_OP_*` in your kernel's `io_uring.h`.
